target_customer: Fans buying and selling tickets to raves, EDM and club nights, starting in New York
problem: Secondary ticket marketplaces focus on seller asking prices and charge heavy fees, which frustrates buyers of scarce rave and club tickets.
business_model: marketplace take rate on peer to peer ticket resale with bid and ask

founders.name: Josh Karol
founders.background_notes: Software engineer at Millennium per YC page

founders.name: Aria Mohseni
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says Mohseni is a DJ

competitors.name: Ticketmaster
competitors.what: dominant primary and resale ticketing platform
competitors.traction_then: market leader, criticized over fees, an antitrust suit and a data breach per TechCrunch

technical_complexity.rationale: A two sided web marketplace with bid and ask matching and payments; standard engineering, web only at launch in January 2024.

defensibility.rationale: Liquidity in a niche scene could build a local network, but the model was copyable by StubHub, SeatGeek or Vivid Seats.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing incumbents copying the EDM niche as of late 2026.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (July 2024) describes buyer frustration with ticket fees and resale platforms that lack buyer intent; the company reported 3,000+ users and about 250 events within months of its January 2024 launch.

identity.logo: Holo style logo and DJ figure artwork seen on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Energetic and nightlife focused, slogan 'No more excuses. You're coming out tonight in New York.'

brand_strength.rationale: Little third party press on the brand itself; only the site shows the style and no naming story was found.

outcome_analysis: CrowdVolt launched in New York in January 2024, raised a reported 1.4 million dollar seed from VC and angel investors, and is still active. Founders are fans of the EDM scene, which gives founder market fit, but the sources do not yet show durable traction or a response from big incumbents, so the outcome is still open.
notes: Aggregators (VCBacked, FundedIQ) show a 500K seed in 2024, and Seedtable a July 2024 raise date; these conflict with the TechCrunch figure and are not recorded. Founder education not found. Outcome search returned nothing about CrowdVolt. Competition: only Ticketmaster is named in a contemporaneous source; other lists were aggregator pages, so not recorded. A yespress profile says Hammer left UBS, unverified secondary source.
